title: Fractal dimension analysis: A new tool for analyzing colony-forming units
author: Nai, Martelli, et al.

steps.title: Gather bacterial strains
steps.instruction: Obtain the following ATCC strains from Microbiologics, Inc.: Escherichia coli ATCC® 25922™, Proteus mirabilis ATCC® 25933™, Staphylococcus aureus subsp. aureus ATCC® 25923™, Staphylococcus epidermidis ATCC® 12228™, and Enterococcus faecalis ATCC® 29212™.

steps.title: Inoculate BHI broth
steps.instruction: Thaw frozen stock aliquots (≈10^8 CFU·mL⁻¹). Pipette 50 µL of each stock into brain‑heart infusion (BHI) broth and mix gently.

steps.title: Incubate bacterial cultures
steps.instruction: Incubate the inoculated BHI tubes at 37 °C for 24 h to obtain overnight cultures.

steps.title: Plate and image colonies
steps.instruction: Spread an appropriate volume of each overnight culture onto blood agar plates containing the prosthetic material (silicone or ePTFE) as described. After incubation, photograph the plates with a digital camera under consistent lighting to obtain images for analysis.

steps.title: Open images in ImageJ
steps.instruction: Launch ImageJ® (http://rsbweb.nih.gov/ij/) and open each captured image file.

steps.title: Convert to 8‑bit
steps.instruction: With the image window active, choose Image → Type → 8‑bit to convert the colour image to an 8‑bit grayscale image.

steps.title: Binarize image
steps.instruction: Select Process → Binary → Make Binary to convert the 8‑bit image to a black‑and‑white (binary) image, where colonies appear as black objects.

steps.title: Run fractal box‑counter
steps.instruction: Choose Analyze → Fractal Box‑Counter. The plugin computes the box‑counting fractal dimension (value between 0 and 2) for the binary image, ignoring texture.

steps.title: Export fractal data
steps.instruction: Save the generated fractal dimension values to a spreadsheet (e.g., .csv). Create a box‑plot of the dimensions if desired.

steps.title: Correlate CFU with fractal dimension
steps.instruction: Using the manual CFU counts and the fractal dimensions, calculate Pearson’s correlation coefficient in SPSS v23.0. Consider results statistically significant when p < 0.05.
